cl_gen_deaths_how_counted.q: How is a death counted as a drug death?
cl_gen_deaths_how_counted.short: Different lists use different rules, so they do not always count the same deaths.
cl_gen_deaths_how_counted.but: The matching studies cover three places. The newest linked data are from 2012.
how: Some lists count drug poisoning as the main cause. Others count drugs found in tests, with age limits.
One death can be counted under several drugs. Finding a drug does not by itself show that it caused the death.
About 49 out of 100 people were on both lists in Norway. Fewer than half were on both in Sweden.
In New Mexico, about 89 out of 100 were on both lists. This study included other poisons too.

cl_gen_deaths_missed.q: Do official counts miss drug deaths?
cl_gen_deaths_missed.short: Some deaths are missing; others are counted without showing which drug was involved.
cl_gen_deaths_missed.but: The gaps differ by place and rules. Most evidence concerns older US opioid deaths.
how: In US records from 1999 to 2015, about 23 out of 100 overdoses had only an unspecified-drug code.
Models guessed which drugs those counted deaths involved. They did not find deaths missing from the total.
In Stockholm, lists with similar totals disagreed about which people to include. They used different rules.
An England and Wales estimate suggests counts held about two thirds of deaths involving each opioid. It did not match each death across lists.

cl_opi_deaths_heroin_missed.q: Do official counts miss heroin deaths?
cl_opi_deaths_heroin_missed.short: Closer file reviews linked more deaths to heroin than certificates or codes did.
cl_opi_deaths_heroin_missed.but: The reviews used their own rules. Their findings do not prove a worldwide missing-death rate.
how: Heroin turns into morphine in the body. Some records said morphine or mixed drugs instead of heroin.
In Maryland, certificates named heroin in about 52 out of 100 deaths the fuller protocol linked to heroin.
In Victoria, about 34 out of 100 model-selected deaths lacked the heroin code. Some were outside the national poisoning definition.
An England and Wales estimate was about half as large again as the count. It combined heroin and morphine and did not match each death.

cl_gen_deaths_autopsy_testing.q: Do autopsies and drug tests change which deaths count as drug deaths?
cl_gen_deaths_autopsy_testing.short: At one US centre, autopsies and drug tests changed the cause, both ways.
cl_gen_deaths_autopsy_testing.but: One North Carolina centre. Its final cause-of-death decisions were not independently checked.
how: At one autopsy centre in North Carolina (2016 to 2021), investigators suspected 2,719 deaths were drug deaths. After a full autopsy and drug tests, about 1 in 10 had another cause, such as a blood clot or a burst blood vessel in the brain.
That 1 in 10 is an upper limit only for the suspected deaths, because it includes deaths where tests found no drug. Of 237 deaths not suspected, the final review classed about half as drug deaths.
In 2018, about 1 in 9 US death investigation offices said they had no access to drug testing (some may send deaths elsewhere), and small offices had it less often than big ones.
Medical examiners' guidance says to do an autopsy whenever a drug death is suspected, but its error figure comes mostly from autopsy studies of all kinds of deaths.

freq.what: of deaths suspected to be drug deaths had another cause after a full autopsy
freq.note: One autopsy centre in North Carolina, 2016 to 2021. An upper limit, and only for the suspected deaths, because it includes deaths where tests found no drug.

cl_gen_deaths_who_investigates.q: Does it matter whether a coroner or a medical examiner investigates?
cl_gen_deaths_who_investigates.short: Not clear. Coroner areas recorded deaths less precisely, but switching showed no clear change.
cl_gen_deaths_who_investigates.but: No study checked which records were right, and the study of switching used data up to 1998.
how: In the US, medical examiners are usually doctors appointed to the job. Coroners are often elected, and in some states need no medical training.

In nine US states (2019 to 2021), deaths in coroner areas were more often recorded without saying whether the death was an accident or a suicide than deaths in medical examiner areas of the same state.
Other US studies found that death certificates named no drug more often where coroners work.
But seven states that switched to medical examiners showed no clear change in how precisely poisoning deaths were recorded, although that study could not rule out a real improvement.

cl_gen_deaths_news_stigma.q: Does how the news describes a drug death change what readers think?
cl_gen_deaths_news_stigma.short: In one study, story details changed how harshly readers judged the person who died.
cl_gen_deaths_news_stigma.but: Readers saw one made-up story and answered straight away; nobody checked what they did later.
how: In 2022, 1,248 adults in the UK each read one made-up news story about a drug death, with the details chosen at random.
Readers judged the person more harshly when the person was a man, was older and had used the drug for years, or had taken heroin rather than ecstasy. The differences were small to moderate.
Support for services that reduce harm, such as drug checking, barely changed.
The study could not tell the effect of age apart from the effect of using the drug for longer.

cl_cath_deaths_news_mephedrone.q: Did news stories about mephedrone deaths get the facts right?
cl_cath_deaths_news_mephedrone.short: Not always: several deaths blamed on it in the news had other causes.
cl_cath_deaths_news_mephedrone.but: One study, and the later test results are second-hand reports, not official records.
how: From late 2009 to around April 2011, online news in the UK linked 18 named deaths to mephedrone.
Later reports said mephedrone was not found in 4, was found but did not cause the death in 4, and played a part in 7, mostly together with other drugs or illnesses.
The two deaths most linked to mephedrone online were later found to be from alcohol and methadone.
Online searches for mephedrone rose when deaths were in the news. The author thinks the news raised interest in the drug, but search data cannot show that the news made people use it.

cl_gen_deaths_level_changes.q: Can drug levels change after death?
cl_gen_deaths_level_changes.short: Yes. Levels can rise or fall and differ between blood vessels.
cl_gen_deaths_level_changes.but: These studies cannot predict the change in one ordinary death.
how: Four selected overdose deaths showed large differences between blood vessels. A medicine given in hospital varied less.
In one person, all imipramine samples after death were about 2 to 8 times the earlier hospital level.
A collection of published reports and Finnish records found that the gap between body samples differs by drug.
Repeated tests found rises for some drugs and falls for others. The first sample was often taken hours after death.

cl_gen_deaths_level_cause.q: Can a blood level show that a drug caused death?
cl_gen_deaths_level_cause.short: Not on its own. Levels overlap between deaths with different causes.
cl_gen_deaths_level_cause.but: The rules and tests used to decide the cause also affect the comparison.
how: In an English autopsy study, MDMA levels in drug deaths overlapped with levels in injury deaths.
An older review reports a similar overlap for morphine. It also cites comparisons with people who survived an overdose.
Finnish data compare blood after death with treatment ranges, not the same people before and after death.
At one US centre, full autopsy changed suspected drug-death classifications in both directions. This study tested drug presence, not levels.

cl_can_deaths_attributed.q: Can cannabis cause a sudden death?
cl_can_deaths_attributed.short: These studies do not settle that question.
cl_can_deaths_attributed.but: The linked deaths are selected reports with no comparison group.
how: A review collected 13 deaths linked to recent use. Eight had significant heart disease or other illness; five lacked a blood test showing recent use.
Larger studies, relayed by the review, point both ways. Some found no increase in deaths.
A Finnish table prints 0% as poisonings mainly attributed to THC, rounded to whole percent. That does not prove an exact zero count.
The reviewers encourage counting cannabis as a contributor in appropriate cases, but give no estimate of missed deaths.

cl_cath_deaths_mephedrone_confirmed.q: How many deaths linked to mephedrone were confirmed?
cl_cath_deaths_mephedrone_confirmed.short: In 25 of 128 alleged deaths, tests after death found no mephedrone.
cl_cath_deaths_mephedrone_confirmed.but: A positive test does not prove cause. A negative test may miss earlier use.
how: By October 2011, 128 deaths in the UK and nearby islands had been linked to mephedrone; 13 results were still pending.
Of 62 deaths studied, mephedrone was the only substance found in 8. Other drugs were common.
One person died weeks later in hospital and had none found after death. Their earlier test evidence is not given.
The authors say tests and incomplete reporting may also miss deaths. They cannot give a death rate.

freq.what: of the 128 alleged deaths had no mephedrone found after death
freq.note: Editors’ rounded calculation: 25/128≈20 in 100; 13 results pending. Negative does not prove no earlier exposure.

cl_opi_deaths_heroin_alone.q: Are heroin overdose deaths always caused by heroin alone?
cl_opi_deaths_heroin_alone.short: Other drugs are often found. That does not show which caused the death.
cl_opi_deaths_heroin_alone.but: These old records cannot tell how many deaths heroin alone caused.
how: In older studies from the USA, Australia and Europe, morphine was the only drug found in 23 to 48 in 100 deaths labelled heroin overdose. Alcohol was found in 29 to 75 in 100.
Many deaths took hours; other people were often present. These are findings relayed by a review.

In England and Wales in 2000, researchers put 23 in 100 reported accidental drug-related deaths in categories beyond direct overdose, under their rules. Methadone was the only drug blamed in 4 in 100 direct overdoses; that does not mean no other drug was found.
Heroin exposure may also be missed when its marker breaks down. Blood levels also depend on the specimen and sampling time.

cl_mdma_deaths_fatal_level.q: What level of MDMA in blood is fatal?
cl_mdma_deaths_fatal_level.short: These studies do not establish a fatal cutoff; the measured levels overlap.
cl_mdma_deaths_fatal_level.but: The groups are small, and some London table decimals are unclear in the scan.
how: In Sheffield, England (1992–2008), levels in deaths attributed to MDMA overlapped levels in injury deaths. The middle value was about 7 times the injury-group value, but was not a cutoff.
The London table values overlap if unclear decimal points have been read correctly. Its survivors included severely ill people, not healthy people after ordinary use.
A Finnish table’s 0% concerns poisoning with MDMA as the main finding, not every possible contribution. It records what certifiers decided.
Sampling time and specimen matter. The London tables do not say when every sample was taken. No study here gives a healthy ordinary-use comparison.

cl_gen_deaths_excited_delirium.short: The label alone does not establish what caused a death.
cl_gen_deaths_excited_delirium.but: The cases were selected for reports. They cannot give the risk per encounter.
how: The reviews describe extreme agitation, but no validated definition or specific autopsy sign. The label is also used with living people.
In 168 published cases, force was recorded in 94 of 104 deaths. That included sedation and electrical weapons as well as physical restraint.
Only 3 cases explicitly had no force; 28 had missing information. A later review also cites deaths attributed to the label without overt restraint.
Researchers disagree about restraint, drugs and the agitated state. These reports cannot tell how much each caused.
